messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 - runtime OOM spike on prod-inference (us-west-2). Affected service: inference-svc-prod. Pager triggered: sustained OOMs on GPU workers 10:14–10:19 UTC. Link: https://internal.incidents/3366994200 :rotating_light:
oncall-ryan: Picking this up. Oncall SRE here. Tagging infra and eng. Any live mitigations in place? :eyes:
alice-sre: joining. Seeing repeated GPU OOM logs and PageAlloc failures. Starting triage. Dropping batch_size on a subset of pods now (canary).
alice-sre: canary command run: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/inference-svc BATCH_SIZE=4 --context=prod` — will monitor.
ben-ml: fyi workload distribution spiked; 95th token length jumped from 512->1400 after a customer rollout 09:55 UTC. Suspect larger seqs + batching = memory pressure.
carla-eng: sharing recent GPU stats (10:12 UTC snapshot):
```
GPU0: total=48GB free=1.8GB used=46.2GB | processes: inference(12) kvcache(2)
GPU1: total=48GB free=2.3GB used=45.7GB | processes: inference(14) kvcache(3)
OOM events: 10:12:13, 10:15:42, 10:16:31
Top alloc callers: forward_pass, kv_cache_restore
```
carla-eng: kv cache resident pages jumped ~x3 after 09:55 due to long-context requests.
infra-bot: Autoscaler: added 2 standby workers to inference-asg at 10:17 UTC (scale up initiated).
oncall-ryan: Good. Maria, can you surface whether any customers saw errors?
maria-support: From error routing: ~1200 requests got 5xx between 10:12–10:19; two customers (acme-inc, healthapp) had >200 failed requests each. Escalated to CSMs.
product-oncall: Noted. Any immediate mitigation beyond batch drop? We need customer impact minimized.
alice-sre: Applying fallback routing for heavy requests: reroute requests with seq_len>1024 to smaller-model-1 (less KV cache) as temporary mitigation. Patch pushed at 10:21 UTC.
ben-ml: Also recommending KV cache eviction aggressiveness increase: from LRU_threshold=0.75 -> 0.60 for canary. That should free resident pages quickly.
carla-eng: running eviction change on canary pod: `curl -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:8080/debug/kvcache/evict?target=0.60` — logs show freed ~6GB on GPU0 at 10:22:03.
carla-eng: new snapshot 10:23 UTC:
```
GPU0: free=8.1GB used=39.9GB
GPU1: free=7.5GB used=40.5GB
```
alice-sre: Observing reduced OOM after eviction on canary. Promoting changes to 30% of fleet.
oncall-ryan: Timeline (so far):
- 09:55 UTC: customer rollout increased long-context traffic
- 10:12 UTC: first OOMs detected
- 10:14 UTC: incident bot paged (P1)
- 10:15-10:19: mitigation attempts (batch_size canary)
- 10:17 UTC: autoscaler added workers
- 10:21 UTC: fallback routing to smaller model
- 10:22–10:23 UTC: KV eviction run, memory reclaimed
- 10:28 UTC: errors trending down

alice-sre: Hypotheses (track):
H1: Long-context requests increased KV resident pages causing fragmentation and peak OOMs. (evidence: kv resident increase at 09:55; forward_pass + kv_restore in top allocs)
H2: Large-batch + long-sequence combinations exceed allocator fragmentation thresholds (evidence: OOMs while overall free memory low but not zero; observed PageAlloc failures)
H3: Regression in KV rehydration path increased async allocations (need deeper logs)

ben-ml: Quick test: reduce GOAL_BATCH_TOKENS from 4096->2048 for canary routing to lower aggregate mem per step. If stable, roll to rest.
carla-eng: logs uploaded: https://logs.internal/3366994200/gpu_metrics.tar.gz (contains per-pod GPU allocations, kv cache snapshots, runtime traces).
carla-eng: grep snippet from runtime.log (10:15:42): `AllocationError: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory at kv_cache_restore.cpp:142`
maria-support: CS notes: acme-inc reported latency + 5xx during window; healthapp flagged model_stall. Both CSMs notified; preparing customer-safe summary.
oncall-ryan: Action items (assign):
- alice-sre: coordinate full rollout of batch reduction + eviction policy across fleet (in-progress).
- carla-eng: collect and attach sticky allocations and allocator telemetry for RCA (assigned).
- ben-ml: run simulation of long-seq + batch combos against current allocator config to reproduce (assigned).
- infra-bot / infra team: evaluate autoscaler thresholds vs burst capacity for inference-asg (assigned).
- product-oncall: prepare customer communication draft (assigned to maria-support for details).

product-oncall: Draft note: short summary + mitigation + ETA for RCA (will share in #customer-updates after SRE + ENG confirm).
alice-sre: Rolling remaining mitigation to 100% now. Monitoring 10:30–10:40 for regression.
carla-eng: One more datapoint: GPU fragmentation index (10:11->10:20): 0.22 -> 0.67 (high). Correlates with inability to satisfy contiguous allocations.
ben-ml: If we can't get stable with batching tweaks, plan B: switch heavy routes to CPU vectorized path (falls back to non-GPU pipeline) for 30m window. Lower perf but avoids OOM.
oncall-ryan: Please keep notes minimal in thread; we will compile a structured RCA doc after incident. For now, keep running commentary here.
alice-sre: Update 10:36 UTC: error rate down to baseline. Closing live mitigation. Moving to postmortem/RC A phase.
carla-eng: Uploaded allocator traces to s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3366994200/allocator_traces.json.gz
ben-ml: Initial conclusion for RCA kickoff: primary cause appears to be combination of long-context traffic spike + batching defaults leading to fragmentation and transient OOMs; kv cache behavior amplified resident memory. Need follow-ups: exact allocator fragmentation modes, eviction tuning, and safer defaults for batch sizing.
oncall-ryan: Thanks all. We'll run a formal RCA meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Assigning doc owner: alice-sre. Please add timeline, raw logs links, hypothesis validation steps, and customer impact section to the RCA doc.
product-oncall: Noted. Maria will draft customer-facing incident summary once RCA owner gives go-ahead. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged resolved (mitigations applied). Incident closed for live ops at 10:40 UTC. Root cause investigation -> RCA in progress.
